comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C27-C32, C84-C86 regarding fentanyl-induced cardiorespiratory depression and nTS activation. Both evaluations find the dose-response data compelling with appropriate controls and statistical analyses. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on claims C33-C36 regarding NLXM biodistribution and peripheral restriction. Both evaluations affirm the pharmacokinetic data and lack of CNS penetration. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on claims C37-C41, C87 regarding NLXM prevention of OIRD. Both evaluations describe this as a central finding with compelling and rigorous evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on claims C79-C82, C96 regarding sex differences. Both evaluations affirm the inclusion of both sexes and appropriate analysis as a strength. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C44-C48 regarding NLXM reversal of OIRD. Both evaluations support the reversal findings as compelling. OpenEval additionally addresses C88, C91, C113 not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C43, C89-C90 regarding nTS activation patterns. Both evaluations support the immunohistochemistry data. Peer review also includes C49-C50, C92 (reversal context) in same result. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial agreement on claims C49-C50, C92 regarding nTS activation after reversal. Both support the finding but peer review groups these with pretreatment nTS data (C42-C43, C89-C90). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C51-C54, C93 regarding lack of aversion with NLXM in CPA experiments. Both evaluations emphasize this as a major therapeutic advantage. Peer review also includes C94-C95 (mechanistic interpretation). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C94-C95, C102 regarding peripheral restriction explaining lack of aversion. OpenEval treats these as mechanistic interpretations (SUPPORTED), while peer review groups them with CPA behavioral findings (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on claims C55-C58, C109-C110 regarding fiber photometry data showing biphasic nTS response. Both acknowledge the data as compelling but OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, requesting additional functional validation of nTS role in OIRD.

Partial overlap on claims C59-C60, C112 regarding temporal dynamics of nTS recovery. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on photometry data, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, requesting functional significance validation for all nTS activity measures.

Disagreement on mechanistic claims C6-C7, C61, C68, C76, C111, C114. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting speculative elements requiring direct validation. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN but emphasizes need for functional nTS manipulation experiments to establish causal relationships.

Partial overlap on main conclusions C4-C5, C8-C9. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about clinical translation. Peer review rates mechanistic understanding (C4, C8) as UNCERTAIN pending functional validation, but affirms therapeutic implications.

Agreement on therapeutic implications C9, C78. Both evaluations affirm significant therapeutic potential despite acknowledging need for clinical validation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer review rates SUPPORTED for therapeutic implications specifically.

Agreement on claim C78 regarding therapeutic potential. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting speculation about clinical translation. Peer review rates SUPPORTED for therapeutic implications while acknowledging work is 'somewhat incremental.'
Agreement on background claims C1-C3, C10-C26. Both evaluations affirm these contextual claims are appropriately supported by literature. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Agreement on literature-based claims C62-C75, C83, C100, C103-C108. Both evaluations affirm appropriate citations and contextual framing. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on methodological limitations C115-C117 regarding anesthesia in photometry experiments. Both evaluations acknowledge this as an appropriate caveat. Both rate as SUPPORTED (as valid methodological considerations).

Agreement on speculative claims C118-C119 regarding mechanisms. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting explicit speculation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, implicitly addressing these through request for functional validation of mechanistic interpretations.

Agreement on claim C101 regarding potential CNS penetration mechanisms. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes it's speculative and untested; peer review does not explicitly address but groups with other uncertain mechanistic claims.
